previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for pleuritic chest pain and concern for pulmonary embolism given her history of recurrent DVT/PE. CT angiography ruled out pulmonary embolism but revealed a new L1 compression fracture and chronic rib fractures. A CT of the sinuses showed acute frontal and chronic maxillary sinusitis, which was treated with levaquin. Her chest pain resolved during the admission. She also reported persistent bloating, attributed to her known gastroparesis, and was continued on metoclopramide and simethicone. Her chronic GVHD, diabetes, and pain from prior fractures were managed with her baseline medications. She remained stable, completed treatment, and was discharged home with follow-up plans.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PA AND LAT)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with CML c/b blast crisis s/p allo transplant
approx ___ years ago c/b GVHD now with worsening dyspnea on exertion.  // Please
evaluate for cause of worsening dyspnea on exertion.

COMPARISON:  ___.

IMPRESSION: 

The lung volumes are low. Moderate cardiomegaly.  Minimal fluid overload but
no overt pulmonary edema.  No evidence of pneumonia.  No pleural effusions on
both the frontal and the lateral radiograph. Moderate tortuosity of the
thoracic aorta.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with bowel distention, evaluate for fecal
loading..

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph ___.  CT abdomen and pelvis ___.

TECHNIQUE  One supine view the abdomen.

FINDINGS: 

There is moderate fecal loading of the ascending colon. There are no dilated
loops of small or large bowel to suggest obstruction. There is no pneumatosis
or secondary evidence of free air. Surgical clips are noted in the right upper
quadrant and right pelvis.

IMPRESSION: 

Moderate fecal loading of the ascending colon.

EXAMINATION:  PELVIS, NON-OBSTETRIC

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with elevated LFTs, distention, lower abdominal
pain  // r/o ovarian cyst/lesion?

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale ultrasound images of the pelvis were obtained with
transabdominal approach followed by transvaginal approach for further
delineation of uterine and ovarian anatomy.

COMPARISON:  Prior CTA chest, abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

The uterus is anteverted and measures 3.2 x 1.7 x 3.0 cm. The endometrium is
homogenous and measures 1 mm.  The ovaries are not identified, but no adnexal
abnormality. There is no free fluid.

IMPRESSION: 

No pelvic mass identified. Ovaries not identified. Normal thickness
homogeneous endometrium.

EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with elevated LFTs, distention  // r/o ascites?
r/o bile duct dilatation?

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Prior CT chest, abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The echogenicity of the liver is homogeneous. The contour of the liver
is smooth. There is no focal liver mass. Main portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.  A tiny calcified granuloma is
identified in the right lobe of the liver.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 2 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: The pancreas is not well assessed owing to overlying bowel gas. A
1.0 cm cyst is identified at the pancreatic head, corresponding to the cystic
lesion seen on prior CT study.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 7.3 cm.

KIDNEYS: The right kidney measures 8.3 cm. A 0.8 cm simple cyst is
incidentally seen at the upper pole of the right kidney, stable since the
prior CT study from ___.

IMPRESSION:


1. Normal echotexture of the liver, with no suspicious focal hepatic lesion
identified. No ascites or intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation. Tiny
calcified granuloma identified in the right lobe of the liver.
2. Pancreas not well assessed, however a 1.0 cm cyst identified in the
pancreatic head corresponding to the cystic lesion seen on prior CT study.
3. 0.8 cm simple cyst at the upper pole right kidney, stable since prior CT
study from ___.

EXAMINATION:  MRA ABDOMEN WANDW/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with persistent abdominal pain  // r/o
mesenteric ischemia? other etiology?

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1 and T2 weighted images were acquired on a 1.5 Tesla
magnet, including dynamic 3D imaging, obtained prior to and following the
uneventful intravenous administration of 0.1 mmol/kg (15 cc) of MultiHance.

 3D postprocessing was performed on an independent workstation, including the
creation of 3D maximum intensity projection images, which support these
findings.

COMPARISON:  MR ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is fatty replacement of the pancreas again noted. Multiple cystic
lesions are again noted in the pancreas including a 2.1 x 1.3 cm cyst in the
pancreatic head (series 7, image 26) previously 1.8 x 1.2 cm. 0.8 x 0.5 cm
lesion is noted in the pancreatic body (series 7, image 20) that is unchanged
from the prior exam. Additional sub 5 mm cysts are again noted, including a 3
mm cyst in the pancreatic body (series 8, image 21) that has decreased in size
from the prior exam.

No hepatic lesion is demonstrated. There is no intra or extrahepatic biliary
dilatation present. The patient has had previous cholecystectomy.  The spleen
is normal size.  The adrenal glands are unremarkable.  There is no
hydronephrosis involving either kidney.

No adenopathy is demonstrated. The visualized loops of small large bowel are
unremarkable.

MRA:  The abdominal aorta is normal caliber. The celiac artery, SMA, renal
arteries, and inferior mesenteric artery are patent, with no stenosis
demonstrated.

T11, L1, and L5 anterior wedge compression fractures are noted.  The L1
compression fracture has developed from the prior exam, and there has been
progression of height loss at T11.  L5 is unchanged. There is no osseous
lesion.

IMPRESSION:



1. Patent mesenteric arteries with no evidence of flow limiting stenosis and
no secondary signs of mesenteric ischemia.
2. Multiple cystic pancreatic lesions are again noted there in keeping with
side branch IPMN. The dominant lesion in the head of the pancreas measures 2.1
x 1.3 cm, slightly increased from the prior exam (previously 1.8 x 1.2 cm). 
Consideration of referral to the pancreas center is recommended. In addition
MRCP followup is recommended in 6 months time to reassess.
3. Multiple anterior wedge compression fractures as described, with a new
compression fracture at L1.

into the Department of Radiology critical communications system for direct
communication to the referring provider.
